title: The sentence bracket and field positions
topic_en: The sentence bracket and field positions
schema: english-prompt -> learner types German -> Reveal/Hide answer shows reference + speaker

exercises.english: At two o'clock, the train arrives at platform five.
exercises.german: Um zwei Uhr kommt der Zug auf Gleis fünf an.
exercises.why: The time adverbial is fronted into position I, so the finite verb kommt follows it and the subject der Zug takes position II; the separable prefix an closes position III.

exercises.english: Yesterday I finally spoke to the landlord.
exercises.german: Gestern habe ich endlich mit dem Vermieter gesprochen.
exercises.why: Fronting Gestern displaces the verb from position I; the perfect auxiliary steht position II and the prefix gesprochen returns to the very end.

exercises.english: It would be much better to come earlier.
exercises.german: Deutlich besser wäre es, früher zu kommen.
exercises.why: A fronted comparative phrase fills position I, which pushes the Konjunktiv II wäre of the copula into position II ahead of the subject es.

exercises.english: Since you are here, I will show you the garden.
exercises.german: Da du hier bist, zeige ich dir den Garten.
exercises.why: The subordinate clause in position I leaves the finite verb of the main clause in position II, which is the second use of the Da-clause.

exercises.english: That he was lying never occurred to me.
exercises.german: Dass er gelogen hat, ist mir nie in den Sinn gekommen.
exercises.why: A fronted dass-clause in position I makes the main clause verb ist occupy position II, while the subject er of the fronted clause stays inside the dass-clause.

exercises.english: Only after three months did she get the visa.
exercises.german: Erst nach drei Monaten hat sie das Visum bekommen.
exercises.why: The fronted temporal phrase Erst nach drei Monaten is emphasised, so the perfect auxiliary hat follows in position II and the subject sie stands behind it.

exercises.english: Despite all the effort, it did not get any better.
exercises.german: Trotz aller Bemühungen ist es nicht besser geworden.
exercises.why: A prepositional phrase with trotz takes position I, and the copula ist of the Perfekt follows in position II before the subject es.

exercises.english: Not a single guest complained about the noise.
exercises.german: Kein einziger Gast hat sich über den Lärm beschwert.
exercises.why: Kein einziger Gast is the fronted subject in position I, so the perfect auxiliary hat, not the subject, comes next.

exercises.english: Where do you actually want to go on holiday?
exercises.german: Wo willst du denn eigentlich in den Urlaub fahren?
exercises.why: The interrogative word wo occupies position I; willst is the finite verb in position II and the subject du follows it.

exercises.english: When the children were small, we lived in the countryside.
exercises.german: Als die Kinder klein waren, lebten wir auf dem Land.
exercises.why: A fronted temporal clause in position I pushes the main-clause verb lebten into position II.

exercises.english: One thing is certain: the figures are not verified.
exercises.german: Eines ist sicher: Die Zahlen sind nicht geprüft.
exercises.why: The nominalised fronted clause Eines ist sicher forms its own bracket, which the colon closes; the following main clause keeps its normal subject-verb order.

exercises.english: Had I known it, I would have cancelled the trip.
exercises.german: Hätte ich es gewusst, hätte ich die Reise storniert.
exercises.why: The Konjunktiv II of haben in position I stands alone, and the subject ich follows it in position II before the main-clause verb.

exercises.english: For exactly this reason the contract was terminated.
exercises.german: Aus genau diesem Grund wurde der Vertrag gekündigt.
exercises.why: The causal phrase is fronted into position I, so the finite part wurde of the passive Perfekt follows, with the subject behind it.

exercises.english: Should the prices rise again, we will react immediately.
exercises.german: Sollten die Preise nochmals steigen, reagieren wir sofort.
exercises.why: The inverted conditional in position I replaces the subject; the Konjunktiv II sollen in position II is followed by the subject wir.

exercises.english: In 1998 she moved to Vienna.
exercises.german: Im Jahr 1998 zog sie nach Wien.
exercises.why: A fronted time expression takes position I, the finite verb zog follows in position II and sie enters the bracket behind it.

exercises.english: Why did nobody warn us?
exercises.german: Warum hat uns niemand gewarnt?
exercises.why: The question word warum is in position I and the perfect auxiliary hat is the finite verb in position II.

exercises.english: What matters is not the prize, but the way you get there.
exercises.german: Entscheidend ist nicht der Preis, sondern der Weg dorthin.
exercises.why: A fronted predicate nominative occupies position I; the linking verb ist goes to position II and the subject folgt after it.

exercises.english: Without that letter, the application would never have succeeded.
exercises.german: Ohne diesen Brief wäre die Bewerbung nie erfolgreich gewesen.
exercises.why: The preposition ohne with its accusative object forms the fronted position I, so the Konjunktiv II wäre of war starts position II.

exercises.english: How gladly she would accept the offer!
exercises.german: Wie gern würde sie das Angebot annehmen!
exercises.why: A fronted exclamation with wie gern introduces an inverted Konjunktiv II würde position II with the subject following it.

exercises.english: Sometime, somewhere, somebody has to have been right.
exercises.german: Irgendwann, irgendwo, irgendjemand muss recht gehabt haben.
exercises.why: Three indefinites are coordinated in position I, and the modal muss is the finite verb in position II with its subject in front of the infinitive haben.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: I will write to you in detail tomorrow.
exercises.german: Ich schreibe dir morgen ausführlich.
exercises.why: The separable prefix schreib- of schreiben leaves the stem in position II, and the adverbial morgen takes the place of the prefix before the end of the clause.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: Have you ever tried our new coffee?
exercises.german: Hast du schon einmal unseren neuen Kaffee probiert?
exercises.why: In the Perfekt the auxiliary hast occupies position II and the participle probiert stands at the end of the clause.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: The train to Hamburg departs at 7:15.
exercises.german: Der Zug nach Hamburg fährt um 7:15 ab.
exercises.why: With a time of departure, the fixed verbal complement abfahren splits: the stem fährt stays in position II and ab goes to position III.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: We are taking the children swimming tomorrow.
exercises.german: Wir nehmen die Kinder morgen zum Schwimmen mit.
exercises.why: The accusative object Kinder fills the middle field and mit, the prefix of mitnehmen, occupies position III at the very end.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: She called her mother in the evening.
exercises.german: Sie ruft am Abend ihre Mutter an.
exercises.why: The temporal phrase stays in the middle field while the separable prefix an- joins the accusative object ihre Mutter at the end.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: Look after the plants while we are away.
exercises.german: Achte auf die Pflanzen, solange wir weg sind.
exercises.why: The imperative stem achte fills position II for the pronoun du, and auf plus its object is the verb complement in the final position.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: You have broken my glasses.
exercises.german: Du hast meine Brille kaputtgemacht.
exercises.why: In the Perfekt the auxiliary hast fills position II and the participle kaputtgemacht has a separable prefix that stands at the clause end.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: The meeting will be postponed by two weeks.
exercises.german: Die Besprechung wird um zwei Wochen verschoben.
exercises.why: The passive auxiliary wird is the finite verb in position II and the participle verschoben, a verb with a separable prefix, goes last.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: Please pick up the parcel at the post office.
exercises.german: Holen Sie bitte das Paket bei der Post ab.
exercises.why: The infinitive of holen drops the prefix ab- into the verb field, and bitte and the accusative object stay in the middle field.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: We didn't arrive in time.
exercises.german: Wir sind nicht pünktlich angekommen.
exercises.why: The negated auxiliary ist stands in position II and the participle angekommen, whose prefix an- detaches, follows it.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: My little brother eats breakfast without me.
exercises.german: Mein kleiner Bruder isst ohne mich Frühstück.
exercises.why: The accusative object Frühstück is the verb complement of essen and moves to position III, after the prepositional phrase ohne mich.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: The children have already gone out.
exercises.german: Die Kinder sind schon nach draußen gegangen.
exercises.why: The directional complement nach draußen is the verb complement of gehen, and the participle gegangen closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: I will call you from the airport.
exercises.german: Ich rufe dich vom Flughafen aus an.
exercises.why: Vom Flughafen aus is a directional complement of anrufen; the prefix an closes position III after it.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: When will you introduce your parents to hers?
exercises.german: Wann stellst du deine Eltern ihren vor?
exercises.why: The prefix vor- of vorstellen separates: stellst is the finite verb in position II and vor moves to the end of the clause.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: Who took the last bottle of water?
exercises.german: Wer hat die letzte Flasche Wasser genommen?
exercises.why: The question word in position I is followed by the perfect auxiliary hat; the strong participle genommen needs no ge- and stands last.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: The council will be dissolved after the vote.
exercises.german: Der Rat wird nach der Abstimmung aufgelöst.
exercises.why: The prefix auf- of auflösen is separated; only the stem löst stands in position II, and the participle aufgelöst ends the sentence.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: My sister has just taken the cake out of the oven.
exercises.german: Meine Schwester hat gerade den Kuchen aus dem Ofen geholt.
exercises.why: A separable verb with a prepositional object places the participle hol- at the very end, after the extended prepositional phrase.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: Please switch off the light when you leave.
exercises.german: Mach bitte das Licht aus, wenn du gehst.
exercises.why: The separable prefix aus- of the imperative attaches to the object das Licht and closes the verb field at the end of the first clause.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: Our guests have already left.
exercises.german: Unsere Gäste sind schon weg.
exercises.why: Weg belongs to the predicate of weggehen and fills the final slot after the auxiliary ist, since the participle merges with the prefix ge-.

exercises.skill: Position III: separable verbs and Perfekt
exercises.english: The parcel will be delivered tomorrow.
exercises.german: Das Paket wird morgen zugestellt.
exercises.why: The passive auxiliary wird occupies position II; the time adverbial morgen stays in the middle field and the participle zugestellt closes position III.

exercises.english: The garden finally bloomed after the rain.
exercises.german: Der Garten blühte endlich, nachdem es geregnet hatte.
exercises.why: A whole subordinate clause occupies the Nachfeld; its finite verb had closes the sentence, because the Nachfeld has no verb field of its own.

exercises.english: We cancelled the appointment, as agreed.
exercises.german: Wir haben, wie besprochen, den Termin abgesagt.
exercises.why: The comment on the manner is inserted in the Nachfeld between the auxiliary and the object, so unlike a fronted comment it does not force inversion.

exercises.english: I sent the report to my boss yesterday.
exercises.german: Ich habe dem Chef gestern den Bericht geschickt.
exercises.why: The dative recipient stays in the middle field while the short accusative object moves into the Nachfeld, leaving the separable prefix geschickt at the very end.

exercises.english: Honestly, I have no appetite for this appointment at all.
exercises.german: Ich habe, ehrlich gesagt, überhaupt keine Lust auf diesen Termin.
exercises.why: The comment on the manner of speaking stands in the Nachfeld, inserted after the auxiliary habe, and the unstressed object stays at the very end.

exercises.english: I haven't had a moment's peace since I signed the contract.
exercises.german: Ich habe, seitdem ich den Vertrag unterschrieben habe, keine Ruhe mehr.
exercises.why: A fronted temporal subordinate clause would force inversion, but placed in the Nachfeld after habe it simply supplements the clause.

exercises.english: On Tuesday the board will decide about the budget.
exercises.german: Der Vorstand entscheidet am Dienstag über das Budget.
exercises.why: The prepositional object über plus its accusative goes into the Nachfeld, because a prepositional phrase normally closes the middle field.

exercises.english: We went to a bar after the concert, as planned.
exercises.german: Wir gingen, wie geplant, nach dem Konzert in eine Bar.
exercises.why: The inserted comment in the Nachfeld licenses the neutral order, in which nach dem Konzert precedes the directional complement in eine Bar.

exercises.english: We received the report, and that already last week.
exercises.german: Wir haben den Bericht bekommen, und zwar schon letzte Woche.
exercises.why: An und zwar phrase can be added in the Nachfeld, which is why the sentence ends with an optional correction rather than with the verb field.

exercises.english: We would get the bicycle for 1,200 euros.
exercises.german: Das Fahrrad würden wir für 1.200 Euro bekommen.
exercises.why: The prepositional phrase für 1.200 Euro sits behind the subject and the modal in the Nachfeld, giving the price the last word.

exercises.english: We will not accept the offer that is already on the table.
exercises.german: Das Angebot, das uns bereits vorliegt, nehmen wir nicht an.
exercises.why: The relative clause is inserted in the Nachfeld after the fronted object, and the prefix of annehmen closes the verb field at the end.

exercises.english: She will finish her diploma thesis next year.
exercises.german: Sie wird ihre Diplomarbeit nächstes Jahr abschließen.
exercises.why: The time expression could occupy the middle field; putting it in the Nachfeld lets the prefixed participle abschließen follow it.

exercises.english: After a long search we finally found a flat.
exercises.german: Wir haben, nachdem wir lange gesucht haben, endlich eine Wohnung gefunden.
exercises.why: The temporal subordinate clause in the Nachfeld expands what happened earlier, while the main clause keeps the usual word order.

exercises.english: He went to the interview against everybody's advice.
exercises.german: Er ist zum Vorstellungsgespräch gegangen, gegen den Rat aller Freunde.
exercises.why: The prepositional phrase sits in the Nachfeld, so the separable prefix of the Perfekt participle can close the sentence directly.

exercises.english: For her birthday I will bake a cake, as always.
exercises.german: Zu ihrem Geburtstag backe ich einen Kuchen, wie immer.
exercises.why: The accusative object already fills the middle field, so the comment on the manner is placed in the Nachfeld after it.

exercises.english: Nothing has changed in the village since then, and that is fine.
exercises.german: Seitdem hat sich im Dorf nichts geändert, und das ist auch gut so.
exercises.why: A whole main clause supplements the first one in the Nachfeld; the first clause closes with its own perfect participle.

exercises.english: Instead of taking the bus, let's take the train.
exercises.german: Statt mit dem Bus zu fahren, nehmen wir lieber den Zug.
exercises.why: An infinitive clause introduced by statt … zu stands in the Nachfeld and ends the sentence, since it forms a bracket with the preposition statt.

exercises.english: Thanks to her advice we found the right address.
exercises.german: Wir haben, dank ihrem Rat, die richtige Adresse gefunden.
exercises.why: The two-part causal phrase dank ihrem Rat is inserted in the Nachfeld and does not disturb the order of the middle field.

exercises.english: The meeting will take place on Friday, as planned.
exercises.german: Das Treffen findet, wie geplant, am Freitag statt.
exercises.why: A comment on the manner of the arrangement is placed in the Nachfeld after the finite verb; fronting it would instead invert the clause.

exercises.english: In my view, she is far too self-confident.
exercises.german: Sie ist, wie ich finde, viel zu selbstbewusst.
exercises.why: The comment on the opinion is inserted in the Nachfeld after the copula ist, which keeps the normal subject-verb order intact.

exercises.english: We are meeting at the main station, as agreed.
exercises.german: Wir treffen uns, wie besprochen, am Hauptbahnhof.
exercises.why: The Nachfeld holds the inserted comment wie besprochen, while the accusative of place remains the final element before the verb field closes.

exercises.english: In my view, we should take the road along the river.
exercises.german: Meiner Meinung nach sollten wir den Flussweg nehmen.
exercises.why: A comment on the opinion can stand in the Nachfeld or in the Mittelfeld, but in position I it licenses subject-verb inversion: sollten wir.

exercises.english: In my opinion, the deadline is unrealistic.
exercises.german: Meines Erachtens ist die Frist unrealistisch.
exercises.why: A genitive comment on the opinion stands in position I; the linking verb ist follows in position II and die Frist comes after it.

exercises.english: As I see it, we have no alternative.
exercises.german: Meiner Ansicht nach haben wir keine Alternative.
exercises.why: A comment on the opinion built on a dative base takes position I, the auxiliary haben forms position II with wir behind it.

exercises.english: For me, that is a complete waste of time.
exercises.german: Für mich ist das eine reine Zeitverschwendung.
exercises.why: Für mich is a comment on the speaker's standpoint; it is followed by the copula ist, and the nominative complement completes the sentence.

exercises.english: Frankly, the project is not worth the money.
exercises.german: Offen gesagt bringt das Projekt sein Geld nicht wert.
exercises.why: A comment on the manner of speaking stands in position I; the main clause then follows with its normal subject-verb order.

exercises.english: To be honest, I forgot about it completely.
exercises.german: Ehrlich gesagt habe ich es völlig vergessen.
exercises.why: The comment on the manner of speaking occupies position I, and the perfect auxiliary habe has to follow it in position II.

exercises.english: Naturally, nobody wants to admit the mistake.
exercises.german: Natürlich will niemand den Fehler zugeben.
exercises.why: The comment stands in position I and the modal will fills position II, with the subject niemand behind it.

exercises.english: In other words, the plan is not realistic.
exercises.german: Mit anderen Worten: Der Plan ist nicht realistisch.
exercises.why: The comment opens the sentence like a demonstrative, so the following main clause keeps the regular order Der Plan ist.

exercises.english: As a consequence, the deadline was extended.
exercises.german: Demzufolge wurde die Frist verlängert.
exercises.why: A comment on the consequence can be fronted, and the passive auxiliary wurde in position II follows it directly.

exercises.english: In my opinion, the price is still too high.
exercises.german: Meiner Ansicht nach ist der Preis immer noch zu hoch.
exercises.why: The dative comment occupies position I; ist in position II is followed by the nominative subject, not by the comment itself.

exercises.english: All things considered, the offer is not bad at all.
exercises.german: Alles in allem ist das Angebot gar nicht schlecht.
exercises.why: A comment on the whole set of aspects is fronted into position I and pushes the copula ist to position II.

exercises.english: I am convinced that the project was worthwhile.
exercises.german: Meiner Überzeugung nach hat sich das Projekt gelohnt.
exercises.why: A comment on a conviction uses the dative, and the perfect auxiliary hat forms position II before the reflexive sich.

exercises.english: If you ask me, the whole thing was a mistake.
exercises.german: Wenn Sie mich fragen, war die ganze Sache ein Fehler.
exercises.why: The comment on a person asked is a conditional clause, and a fronted wenn-clause in position I forces inversion: war die ganze Sache ein Fehler.

exercises.english: Obviously, the results speak for themselves.
exercises.german: Offensichtlich sprechen die Ergebnisse für sich.
exercises.why: A comment on how obvious something is is fronted; the main clause then begins with its subject and verb sprechen.

exercises.english: From my experience, such plans rarely work out.
exercises.german: Nach meiner Erfahrung bringen solche Pläne selten etwas.
exercises.why: The comment on experience is a prepositional phrase with the dative; fronted, it is followed by the finite verb bringen.

exercises.english: In my assessment, the deadline was badly calculated.
exercises.german: Nach meiner Einschätzung war die Frist viel zu knapp bemessen.
exercises.why: A comment on the assessment is fronted into position I, so the finite verb war enters position II ahead of the subject.

exercises.english: By my reading, the treaty was signed in 1998.
exercises.german: Meines Erachtens wurde der Vertrag 1998 unterzeichnet.
exercises.why: A genitive comment on the opinion occupies position I; the passive auxiliary wurde takes position II, with the subject after it.

exercises.english: Basically, that is a decision against the project.
exercises.german: Im Grunde ist das eine Entscheidung gegen das Projekt.
exercises.why: A comment on the way something is done stands in position I; the linking verb ist in position II is followed by the nominative complement.

exercises.english: It seems that everything points in the same direction.
exercises.german: Es scheint, dass alles in dieselbe Richtung zeigt.
exercises.why: The comment Es scheint, dass opens the clause like a demonstrative, so the subordinate clause behind it keeps its own field structure.

exercises.english: Quite frankly, that would be a mistake.
exercises.german: Ganz ehrlich gesagt wäre das ein Fehler.
exercises.why: A comment on the manner of speaking stands in position I, the Konjunktiv II wäre in position II, and das completes the bracket.

exercises.english: The more you practise, the more fluent you become.
exercises.german: Je mehr du übst, desto sicherer wirst du.
exercises.why: The je-clause stands in position I with its verb übst; after desto the main clause must invert to wirst du, not du wirst.

exercises.english: The longer the seminar lasts, the more expensive it becomes.
exercises.german: Je länger das Seminar dauert, desto teurer wird es.
exercises.why: The comparative je-clause fills position I, and the second half inverts so that the verb wird comes before the subject es.

exercises.english: The more we practise, the fewer mistakes we make.
exercises.german: Je mehr wir üben, desto weniger Fehler machen wir.
exercises.why: A negated comparative in the second half; the inversion after desto places machen, the finite verb, in front of wir.

exercises.english: The earlier you book, the cheaper it will be.
exercises.german: Je früher du buchst, desto billiger wird es.
exercises.why: The je-clause carries the finite verb buchst in position I, and the second clause with desto inverts to wird es.

exercises.english: The harder she tried, the more she learned.
exercises.german: Je mehr sie sich anstrengte, desto mehr lernte sie.
exercises.why: A verb with a reflexive pronoun in position I; the second half after desto again puts the finite verb lernte before its subject.

exercises.english: The colder it gets, the more firewood we need.
exercises.german: Je kälter es wird, desto mehr Holz brauchen wir.
exercises.why: The subject es in the je-clause comes after the comparative; the second half inverts to brauchen wir.

exercises.english: The more time you have, the better you can prepare.
exercises.german: Je mehr Zeit du hast, desto besser kannst du dich vorbereiten.
exercises.why: The modal verb in position II of the je-clause is kannst; after desto the second main clause inverts to kannst du.

exercises.english: The later you go to sleep, the harder it is to get up.
exercises.german: Je später du zu Bett gehst, desto schwerer fällt dir das Aufstehen.
exercises.why: The separable prefix ge- of gehen moves to position III; the second half inverts to fällt dir das Aufstehen.

exercises.english: The more people join, the better the event will be.
exercises.german: Je mehr Leute mitmachen, desto besser wird die Veranstaltung.
exercises.why: A prefix verb mitmachen keeps its prefix in position I; the second half inverts to wird die Veranstaltung.

exercises.english: The deeper the roots, the more stable the tree.
exercises.german: Je tiefer die Wurzeln reichen, desto standfester wird der Baum.
exercises.why: The je-clause with a final verb reichen is the first member of the comparison; the second member must invert to wird der Baum.

exercises.english: The less you plan, the more chaos you will cause.
exercises.german: Je weniger du planst, desto mehr Chaos verursachst du.
exercises.why: The je-clause in position I with verb planst; the second half inverts to verursachst du, not du verursachst.

exercises.english: The faster you read, the less you remember.
exercises.german: Je schneller du liest, desto weniger erinnerst du dich.
exercises.why: A reflexive pronoun in the second half: the inversion places the finite verb erinnerst before the subject du, and the dative sich follows.

exercises.english: The more one travels, the less one fears the unknown.
exercises.german: Je mehr man reist, desto weniger fürchtet man das Unbekannte.
exercises.why: The impersonal man is a subject and stays in position II; the second half inverts to fürchtet man.

exercises.english: The longer you wait, the more you lose.
exercises.german: Je länger man wartet, desto mehr verliert man.
exercises.why: A parallel je-clause with man as subject; the verb in position I is wartet, and after desto the main clause inverts to verliert man.

exercises.english: The more you know, the fewer questions you ask.
exercises.german: Je mehr du weißt, desto weniger fragst du.
exercises.why: The second comparative is negated; the inversion after desto gives fragst du, which also happens to end in -st.

exercises.english: The earlier you start, the more buffer you have.
exercises.german: Je früher du anfängst, desto mehr Puffer hast du.
exercises.why: The prefix an- of anfangen separates in position I, where only the finite verb fängst appears; the second half inverts to hast du.

exercises.english: The more we cut corners, the more errors appear.
exercises.german: Je mehr wir abkürzen, desto mehr Fehler entstehen.
exercises.why: The je-clause with abkürzen in position I; the second half inverts to entstehen, with Fehler as its subject.

exercises.english: The greater the effort, the greater the reward.
exercises.german: Je größer der Aufwand ist, desto größer der Erfolg.
exercises.why: The main clause in the second half leaves out the auxiliary entirely, so ist is the only finite verb and der Erfolg follows it.

exercises.english: The more you train, the better you play.
exercises.german: Je mehr du trainierst, desto besser spielst du.
exercises.why: Both halves carry a finite verb of their own; the second one inverts to spielst du, which is the reverse of du spielst.

exercises.english: The more generously she donates, the more she is thanked.
exercises.german: Je großzügiger sie spendet, desto mehr wird ihr gedankt.
exercises.why: The passive in the second half is inverted into position II: wird ihr gedankt, with the dative object and the participle behind it.
